gloss: to burn in; to sear into memory; to imprint

forms.label: Past polite
forms.negative: {焼|や}き{付|つ}けませんでした

forms.label: ている past
forms.negative: {焼|や}き{付|つ}けていなかった

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {焼|や}き{付|つ}けていませんでした

definitions.explanation: To burn an image or mark onto something.

definitions.gloss: to sear into memory; to imprint
definitions.explanation: To make a strong impression that stays in one's mind.

examples.japanese: その{光景|こうけい}は{目|め}に{焼|や}き{付|つ}いている。
examples.english: That scene is seared into my eyes.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}の{笑顔|えがお}を{心|こころ}に{焼|や}き{付|つ}けた。
examples.english: I imprinted her smile in my heart.

examples.japanese: {鉄|てつ}に{印|しるし}を{焼|や}き{付|つ}ける。
examples.english: To brand a mark onto iron.

examples.japanese: {牛|うし}に{焼印|やきいん}を{焼|や}き{付|つ}ける。
examples.english: To brand cattle with a branding iron.

examples.japanese: {木|き}の{板|いた}に{模様|もよう}を{焼|や}き{付|つ}けた。
examples.english: I burned a pattern into a wooden board.

examples.japanese: {最後|さいご}の{試合|しあい}を{目|め}に{焼|や}き{付|つ}けておきたい。
examples.english: I want to sear the final game into my memory.

notes:
・{焼|や}き{付|つ}ける → {焼|や}き{付|つ}けない (negative)
・{焼|や}き{付|つ}ける → {焼|や}き{付|つ}けて (te-form)
・{焼|や}き{付|つ}ける → {焼|や}き{付|つ}けた (past)

FORMATION:
Compound verb: {焼|や}く (to burn) + {付|つ}ける (to attach)

USAGE:
Often used in the intransitive form {焼|や}き{付|つ}く:
・{目|め}に{焼|や}き{付|つ}く (to be seared into one's eyes)
・{心|こころ}に{焼|や}き{付|つ}く (to be imprinted on one's heart)
・{記憶|きおく}に{焼|や}き{付|つ}く (to be burned into memory)

The metaphorical sense (sense 2) is more common in everyday speech.
